<header>Sūtrasthāna, Chapter 19. (143)</header>

Having thoroughly removed the impurities, place the patient in position. The skilled physician should repeatedly cleanse the impurities from wounds caused by <term>kapha</term> <gloss>phlegm humor</gloss> and <term>vāyu</term> <gloss>air/wind humor</gloss> through gentle suction. 39. Pressing the wound from below, allow the fluids to drain in the direction of the hair follicles, and properly unite all hidden bindings (connections) and joints. 40. In connecting the lips, follow the procedures previously described. A physician knowledgeable in anatomy should also apply appropriate bandages to bone fractures, using their own judgment. 41.

The wound does not become aggravated for a person who is rising, sitting, going to bed, walking, or riding various vehicles. 42. Wounds located in joints, bones, internal cavities, veins, and ligaments, as well as those that are deeply embedded, profound, or unevenly positioned in all directions, cannot be successfully treated without appropriate bandaging. 43.

Thus concludes the eighteenth chapter of the Sūtrasthāna in the Suśruta Saṃhitā. 18.

A wound does not cause pain to someone who is rising, sitting, lying down, walking, or riding, provided it is bandaged as described. 42. Wounds found in joints, bones, or visceral organs, those in veins and nerves, deep and profound wounds, and those that are irregular on all sides cannot be healed without the aforementioned bandages. 43.

Thus concludes the Hindi commentary by Pandit Muralidhar Sharma on the eighteenth chapter of the Sūtrasthāna of the Suśruta Saṃhitā. 18.

### Chapter Nineteen. 19.

Now, we shall explain the chapter concerning the care and conduct of the wounded patient.

Here, we begin the explanation of the <term>Vraṇitopāsanīya</term> <gloss>chapter on the regimen for the wounded</gloss>.

First, one should select a dwelling for the wounded patient; that dwelling should be auspicious in its location and construction. 1. In a house with a favorable environment that is clean and free from direct sunlight and strong winds, there will be no physical, traumatic, or mental illnesses. 2. In that place, one should provide a bed that is not crowded, well-spread, pleasant, and positioned with the head toward the east, accompanied by weapons for protection. 3. The patient will be comfortable in movement on a well-spread bed. The gods reside in the eastern direction, so the head should be bowed toward them in worship. 4.

<note>Footnote: (Verse 42) tied with bandages.</note>

<summary>This page concludes the eighteenth chapter regarding wound management and bandaging, and begins the nineteenth chapter, which details the appropriate environment and living conditions for a wounded patient to ensure recovery.</summary>
